description: Payloads and the schema_version that oldest-that-fits assigns them against the registered set in registry/schemas.json. 'satisfies' lists every registered version the payload validates under, with no coercion and no members the schema does not name; 'schema_version' is the smallest of them, always. Because schema_version sits inside the envelope and therefore inside block_id, two implementations that chose differently here would compute different names for identical knowledge and stop sharing blocks without either of them failing.

vectors.name: semantic_satisfying_several_takes_the_oldest

payload.label: Fourier
payload.statement: a periodic function decomposes into sines and cosines

vectors.canonical_bytes: {"boltzmann":1,"memory_type":"semantic","payload":{"kind":"formula","label":"Fourier","statement":"a periodic function decomposes into sines and cosines"},"schema_version":1,"serialization":"jcs/1"}
vectors.why: The case the rule exists for. This payload validates under more than one registered schema, and the oldest is chosen: writing it under the newest would silently re-version every block written after a schema is registered, including blocks using nothing it added.

vectors.name: semantic_using_a_later_vocabulary_takes_that_version
vectors.why: A brain stops being readable by an older client exactly at the point where it genuinely uses something that client has no schema for -- and not one block earlier.

vectors.name: episodic_minimal_takes_the_oldest
vectors.why: The same rule in a second memory type: registration number decides, never recency.

vectors.name: procedural_minimal_takes_the_oldest
vectors.why: A procedure that uses no later vocabulary stays readable by the oldest client that knows procedures.

vectors.name: provenance_naming_nobody_stays_at_one
vectors.note: Version 2 removes a required member rather than adding one, so the two are disjoint rather than nested. A payload carrying producer satisfies version 1 alone.

vectors.name: provenance_naming_who_assisted_takes_two
vectors.note: And the mirror: a payload carrying assisting parties satisfies version 2 alone. Oldest-that-fits needs no new rule for a removal, because 'satisfies' already admits no member a schema does not name.

vectors.name: provenance_carrying_both_is_refused
vectors.note: producer belongs to version 1 and assisted_by to version 2; a payload with both satisfies neither, and a writer that meant one of them must say which.

vectors.name: provenance_carrying_neither_is_refused
vectors.note: Version 1 obliged a writer to say what produced a derived block. Dropping producer must not quietly relax that into 'derived, and I decline to say by what', so version 2 requires the parties instead.
